output.content:
**Marvell Technology — Q4 FY2026 (quarter ended January 31, 2026)**

- Marvell reported record Q4 revenue of **$2.219 billion**, up **7% sequentially** and **22% year over year**; this was **$19 million above** the midpoint of its December guidance. [[1]]
- Q4 GAAP net income was **$396.1 million**, or **$0.46 per diluted share**, while non-GAAP net income was **$685.1 million**, or **$0.80 per diluted share**. [[1]]
- Q4 data-center revenue was a record **$1.651 billion**, up **9% sequentially** and **21% year over year**, accounting for roughly **74%** of company revenue. [[1]] [[2]]
- Management attributed the data-center outperformance to stronger-than-expected demand across its **interconnect** portfolio, with sequential growth in **optical interconnects/electro-optics, custom silicon, switching, and storage**. [[2]]
- Communications and other revenue was **$567.4 million**, up **2% sequentially** and **26% year over year**. [[1]]

**Custom AI silicon**

- Marvell’s custom business generated approximately **$1.5 billion in FY2026 revenue**, roughly **doubling year over year**; FY2026 was the first full production year for the relevant custom programs. [[2]]
- The company characterized custom silicon as about **25% of data-center revenue** over the recent period, versus optical interconnect at roughly half, illustrating that Marvell’s AI exposure is meaningfully split between compute silicon and connectivity rather than resting solely on custom XPUs. [[3]]
- For FY2027, management expected custom-business revenue to increase by **more than 20%**, with multiple XPU-attach programs ramping; it expected the business to at least double again in FY2028. [[2]]
- The principal investment implication is that Q4 showed custom silicon continuing to scale, but the near-term data-center upside was led especially by connectivity demand rather than a single custom-silicon program. [[2]]

**Electro-optics / interconnect**

- Marvell’s interconnect franchise—including electro-optics—was the primary source of Q4 upside, and management expected its data-center interconnect business to grow **more than 50% year over year in FY2027**, above its prior approximately 30% expectation. [[2]] [[4]]
- Optical interconnect had compounded at approximately **50% annually for five consecutive years** and represented roughly **half of Marvell’s data-center revenue**, according to the company’s FY2026 filing. [[3]]
- The technology roadmap included transition toward **1.6T optical interconnect**, alongside continued demand for 800G-class connectivity; the company had previously begun shipments of its 1.6T PAM DSP. [[5]]
- Thus, electro-optics remains Marvell’s largest data-center product pillar and a key near-term growth engine, while custom AI silicon supplies the longer-duration XPU and XPU-attach expansion opportunity. [[3]] [[2]]

**Outlook**

- Marvell guided Q1 FY2027 total revenue to **$2.400 billion, plus or minus 5%**, implying continued expansion from Q4. [[1]]
- It expected Q1 FY2027 data-center revenue to grow approximately **10% sequentially** and FY2027 data-center revenue to rise roughly **40% year over year**. [[2]]
- FY2026 total revenue was **$8.195 billion**, up **42% year over year**, while full-year data-center revenue surpassed **$6 billion**, up **46%**. [[1]] [[2]]
